sections.heading: 1. How to adjust
lines: ① Ease back on wide-grip bench and deep dips.
② Keep everything else going as usual.
③ Build biceps, cuff and shoulder blade strength.
④ Add weight, range or speed, one at a time.

or a new bulge in the upper arm.

slides.heading: Get it checked if you notice

caption:
That nagging ache right at the front of your shoulder during bench or chin-ups? The biceps tendon is often involved.

It tends to flare with a jump in overhead or pressing work, heavy carrying, or alongside other shoulder niggles. Most people don't need to stop training. Easing back on the lifts that provoke it while keeping everything else going usually works better than full rest.

From there, gradual strengthening for the biceps, rotator cuff and shoulder blade muscles does the heavy lifting.

A sudden pop with bruising, or a new bulge in the upper arm, is worth getting checked. Our Sydney CBD and Chatswood physios can help you keep lifting. Book online via the link in bio.
